subject: Staged hotfix runway + quiet-window for VPC private fleets
messages:
From: Jordan Price <ops@acmecloud.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: support@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-09-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: private fleet instability during rolling upgrades

Naomi —

Quick summary: during last Sunday's rolling upgrade two of our pinned VPC nodes hit extended stall (~6–8 mins) while the KV cache refill was happening. Customer-facing latency spiked and we had to abort the wave. We need a hardened hotfix plan for our Private customers that:

- lets us apply critical microfixes with a guaranteed minimal blast radius
- defines a quiet window and exact rollback runway so our SREs can act fast
- accounts for network flaps in the customer overlay (we saw intermittent ARP storms)

Can your team propose a concrete staged hotfix runway and any network-level mitigations we should ask customers to do ahead of time? I'll need something we can run with AcmeCloud SOC and our NOC this week.

Attaching the partial logs and the patch bundle we tested.

Jordan
Ops Lead, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme-logs-0923.zip (log bundle), acme-test-patch.tar.gz (tested binary)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged hotfix runway + quiet-window for VPC private fleets

Jordan — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I reviewed the traces and the failure pattern points to two correlated issues:

1) KV cache refill pause combined with a degraded NIC path (we saw RX drops on the secondary uplink).
2) The rolling wave doesn't enforce a per-pod circuit-breaker cooldown, so subsequent nodes are primed and hit the same resource pressure.

Proposal (high level):
- Staged hotfix runway: canary -> staggered wedge -> fleet wave -> monitoring hold -> release.
  - Canary: 2 pods in an isolated AZ (30–45m).
  - Staggered wedge: 10% of fleet with 20m spacing and KV cache warm-up verification.
  - Fleet wave: 40% then 50% after successful hold windows.
- Quiet window (customer ask): schedule a 3.5 hour window with the first 90 minutes reserved for canary + wedge. This gives us runway to abort and rollback if we see KV refill regressions.
- Rollback runway: allow a 30 minute automated rollback for any wave that registers >3x baseline error rate or >1.5x latency for >5 minutes. Manual override for SRE after that.
- Network mitigations to recommend to customers before starting: confirm BGP flap buffers are set, remove any nonstandard VLAN tagging on compute plane, and place the control-plane hosts on a prioritized queue (QoS) during the window.

I've attached a compact runbook excerpt and the patch notes (hotfix_patch_notes_v2.pdf). Karthik and Monica — can you review the abort thresholds and the KV warmup checks? Rafael, can you comment on the recommended NIC/ARPs workaround?

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior TPM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hotfix_patch_notes_v2.pdf, canary-run-matrix.csv
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-23T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged hotfix runway + quiet-window for VPC private fleets

Naomi — quick read and a couple concrete asks/changes:

- Abort/rollback thresholds: tighten the latency window to trigger at 3 minutes sustained at 1.3x baseline (instead of 5m at 1.5x). The shorter detection window gives us faster rollback and reduces customer impact.
- KV warm-up verification: add a token-pressure metric check (token-eviction-rate) and require it to be <5% for two consecutive 1-minute buckets before progressing to next wedge.
- For the stagger timing: reduce wedge spacing to 12–15m for 10% waves (we can parallelize some of the KV pre-warm tasks) — but increase canary observation to 45m.

I'll update the canary-run-matrix.csv with these thresholds. Also: add a health-check hook that validates control-plane connectivity (TLS handshake time) against a synthetic probe; if handshake time increases by >200ms, trigger a soft stop.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

Subject: Re: Staged hotfix runway + quiet-window for VPC private fleets

Adding the runbook excerpt and an ops checklist we should push to customers. Two small additions:

- Preflight checklist for customers (ask to complete 48h prior):
  * Verify KMS connectivity from control plane to customer-managed HSM (if used) — a single TLS handshake failure can block health probes.
  * Confirm overlay MTU consistent across all compute nodes; mismatched MTU was a contributor in the ARP storm case.
  * Provide NOC contact reachable during the entire quiet window and a secondary emergency contact.

- Escalation steps in order:
  1) Pause next wave and initiate rollback to pinned version (we keep previous pin for 24h).
  2) Execute network mitigation playbook (attachment: network-diff.txt shows the suggested iptables and ARP throttling knobs).
  3) If rollback doesn't clear issues in 20m, call in customer network team and consider isolating the node (cordon + evacuate) and rescheduling.

I'll add these to the shared Drive doc. Bottom line: agreed on Naomi's runway but adopt Karthik's tighter detection windows and my 48h preflight for customers.

— Monica
Software Ops Lead, Private Deployments

Attachments referenced: network-diff.txt
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Jordan Price <ops@acmecloud.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-24T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged hotfix runway + quiet-window for VPC private fleets

Jordan — quick alignment from the networking side. Two practical mitigations we recommend AcmeCloud apply before the window:

1) Short-term ARP damping: configure vendor ARP suppression to a 5s damping period for compute VLANs serving our pods; this reduces ARP storms during NIC flaps.
2) Secondary uplink backoff: move secondary NIC to passive mode for the window (keeps primary path exclusively for control-plane traffic).

If those aren't possible, we can insert a temporary eBPF attach on the node to drop duplicate ARP broadcasts for the duration of the maintenance. That has the lowest blast radius and is reversible.

I'll be available on the maintenance call. Once you confirm the Friday quiet window (propose: 2028-09-29 22:00–01:30 UTC), we'll publish the runbook and schedule the canary.

— Rafael
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
